DXF6RrxjhFh.content: DoorDash Driver Highlights Impact of Trump's 'No Tax on Tips' Policy After White House Delivery A DoorDash driver who recently delivered a McDonald's order to the White House says she has personally benefited from President Donald Trump's "no tax on tips" policy included in his broader tax and border legislation. Sharron Simmons, who said she has been delivering with DoorDash since 2022, described the experience as both historic and financially meaningful after becoming the first DoorDash driver to deliver a meal to the White House. Simmons said the tax policy has increased her take-home income and estimated she could save between $3,000 and $4,000 under the current rules. The measure is part of Trump's "One Big Beautiful Bill," a legislative package that includes tax relief for tipped workers, temporary elimination of taxes on overtime pay, and an increase in the child tax credit. Supporters argue the policy helps workers keep more of their earnings and stimulates economic activity. Critics, however, warn that the tax cuts could reduce government revenue and add pressure to the federal deficit. Simmons said she hopes the no-tax-on-tips provision will continue beyond its current expiration date in 2028 but added she plans to benefit from the policy while it remains in place.
